headline: Warm, sunny Santa Ana weather continues Friday, then the pattern flips to cool and wet next week, led by a strong storm that could start as early as Monday night or Tuesday morning with 1 to 3 inches of rain on the coast, 3 to 5 inches in the mountains, possible thunderstorms and strong winds.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thanksgiving was a standout warm day, with highs in the low to mid 80s across the coasts and valleys of Los Angeles and Ventura counties, including the Glendale area, and the mid to upper 70s in San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties, 8 to 12 degrees above normal. Santa Ana (dry northeast offshore) winds kept humidity at just 15 to 25 percent. Tonight stays clear and dry, with a Wind Advisory continuing for some areas until 9 AM Friday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday looks similarly warm and sunny, with highs peaking in the upper 70s to mid 80s before the offshore winds start to weaken; some northeast winds return but are weaker and mostly limited to the Santa Susana and Santa Lucia ranges. It stays dry through Saturday, with cooling beginning over the weekend. A very weak first storm Sunday afternoon into Monday morning may not even bring measurable rain everywhere, with at most about a tenth of an inch.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The storm door is open next week, with at least two more storms. The second, much stronger storm now looks at least 12 hours sooner, with rain starting as early as Monday night or Tuesday morning; it carries unusually high moisture for a winter storm, and models agree well on a high chance of heavy rain, roughly 1 to 3 inches on the coast and 3 to 5 inches in the mountains. Thunderstorms are a good possibility, severe weather is possible, and some long-range guidance shows winds over 50 mph at the storm's peak, so residents near areas burned in the last year or two should watch the forecast closely. A third, much weaker storm is expected later in the week.

coast: A large, long-period west swell slowly eases tonight through Friday night. Exceptionally high tides of 7.4 to 7.7 feet Friday morning bring moderate coastal flooding to low-lying spots on the Central Coast from Point Conception northward and the Ventura and Los Angeles County coasts, with minor flooding possible elsewhere; tides up to 7.2 feet Saturday morning keep moderate flooding going on the Ventura County coast around the late-morning high tide. Coastal Flood Advisories run until 4 PM Friday for many beaches and until 2 PM Saturday for the Ventura County beaches, High Surf Advisories run until 3 PM or 9 PM Saturday depending on the stretch of coast, and a Beach Hazards Statement covers other beaches through Saturday afternoon. Expect strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, sneaker waves, heavy shore break and coastal erosion, making swimming dangerous. On the water, Small Craft Advisories run until 3 AM Friday, 3 PM Friday or 3 AM Saturday depending on the area, with near-advisory offshore winds from Point Mugu to Santa Monica tonight and rough seas on the outer waters and north of Point Sal into Friday night. Conditions are mostly calmer Saturday through Monday, then winds rise to advisory levels Monday evening and to gale force late Monday night through Tuesday night, with large, increasingly hazardous seas as the strong storm arrives.
watch_for: Timing and strength of the strong midweek storm, which could start as early as Monday night or Tuesday morning
Heavy rain, possible thunderstorms and 50+ mph gusts near recent burn areas
Coastal flooding at Friday's and Saturday's morning high tides in low-lying, unprotected spots
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the warm, dry weather through Saturday and say no forecast changes were needed tonight; they see good model agreement on a strong midweek storm with a high chance of heavy rain while cautioning that its timing and strength can still shift 4 to 5 days out, and have moderate to high confidence in the marine forecast.
